the solvent mixture containing ethanol, diethyl-ether and water in the ratio of 8:1:2 is most effective in extracting phenolics and antioxidant compounds from pomegranates arils.

the solvent mixture of ethanol, diethylether and water (8.0:1.0:1) is the most efficient solvent combination for extracting the major antioxidant compounds, especially punicalagins, gallic acid and ellagic acid from pomegranates.

the combination of ethanol, ether and water (E/E/W, 8:1:2, v/v/v) is the most effective solvent to extract phenolic compounds from the pomegranate peel and the extract exhibited high antioxidant activity.

the combination of ethanol, acetone, and water (8 : 1 : 1) extract exhibited higher antioxidant activity and total phenolic content than that of the other extracts.
the combination of ethanol, water and diethyl ether (8:1.1) is the most effective solvent to extract the major phenolics from the pomegranate.
pomegranates are rich in phenolic compounds with antioxidant activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the extraction of polyphenols is a complex process and the solvent system plays an important role in extraction of different polyphenols with different antioxidant properties.
a combination of solvents is more effective than a single solvent for extracting polyphenols with high antioxidant activity from pomegranates.

the combination of solvents is a good approach for extraction of bioactive compounds from plant material and it is also important to understand the role of solvent system in extraction of bioactive components.
